title: Parnassos & Arachova: Skiing Above the Oracle
subRegion: Mount Parnassos, Arachova & Delphi, Central Greece

bestPeriod.window: Late January-late February, the only weeks in which Parnassos can be relied on to have both sectors open
bestPeriod.avoid: 24 December-6 January, when Arachova doubles in price and the access road gridlocks; and after mid-March, when the mountain is usually finished regardless of what the calendar says
bestPeriod.raw: Late January-late February, the only weeks in which Parnassos can be relied on to have both sectors open

accommodation.note: Arachova guesthouses €70, €140 per room; Delphi and Polydrosos 30-40% less

food.note: Taverna mains €10, €18; tsipouro €4, €6; mountain canteen food is poor and overpriced, eat in the villages

transport.note: Hire car €35, €55/day plus fuel and tolls; snow chains are a legal requirement, budget for hire

activities.note: Lift tickets €20 weekday / €35 weekend, Delphi site and museum, one guided snowshoe day

profile.difficultyNote: 3/5, four short lift-served days on modest vertical, plus a snowshoe day on the Livadi plateau and a lot of walking at Delphi; the demand is weather patience, not fitness

gatewayAirport: ATH Athens Eleftherios Venizelos, 200 km / 2 h 30-3 h to Arachova; the ski centre is a further 27 km / 35-45 min above the town
summary: Parnassos is the strangest ski week in Europe, and the reason to do it is not the skiing. It is the fact that you can spend a morning on a lift-served bowl at 2,200 m looking south over the Gulf of Corinth, and an afternoon walking the Sacred Way at **Delphi**, ten kilometres down the mountain, where the Greeks located the centre of the world. **Arachova**, a vertical stone village at 950 m clinging to the mountainside between the two, has spent thirty years turning itself into Greece's winter social capital, the ratio of fur coats to ski boots in its bars on a Saturday night is genuinely remarkable. The ski centre itself is state-run, with two linked sectors, **Kelaria** and **Fterolakka**, a third at **Gerontovrachos**, and Greece's first and only gondola lifts. The honest framing is this: the mountain is small, the season is short, the snow is unreliable, and you must build the week so that a bad snow report does not ruin it. This itinerary therefore alternates ski days with Delphi, the Corycian Cave, the north-side villages of **Agoriani/Eptalofos** and **Polydrosos**, and the tsipouro-and-formaela circuit, so that skiing is the bonus, not the premise.

itinerary.title: Athens to Arachova, and the first look at the mountain
itinerary.morning: Land at **ATH** and pick up a hire car. **Confirm the car has snow chains and that you know how to fit them before you leave the airport**, on the Parnassos access road they are a legal requirement in snow conditions and the police turn cars back without them.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive northwest, roughly 200 km and 2 h 30-3 h via Thiva and Livadeia, climbing the last stretch to **Arachova** at 950 m. Check in, then walk up the **264 steps to Agios Georgios** at the top of the village for the view down the Pleistos gorge toward the Gulf of Corinth.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at **Taverna Dasargyris**, the village's long-standing kitchen, order the **formaela** fried at the table, kokoretsi if it is on, and a carafe of **tsipouro**. Then check tomorrow's snow report at snowreport.gr before you sleep.
itinerary.dayStats: ATH-Arachova ≈ 200 km / 2 h 30-3 h / Arachova 950 m / snow chains legally required on the access road / Delphi 10 km west

itinerary.title: Kelaria: the gondola, and learning the mountain
itinerary.morning: Drive the 27 km up to **Kelaria**, 35-45 minutes and around 800 m of climb, on a road that is properly maintained but genuinely alpine. Arrive before 09:00 on a weekday and the car park is empty. Buy the **weekday ticket at €20**, or **€35 if it is a weekend or holiday**, with **5% off if you buy online**.
itinerary.afternoon: Ride the **Ermis gondola**, the first gondola built in a Greek ski resort, and spend the day working the Kelaria blues and reds. The terrain is wide, sunny and forgiving; the views south over the Gulf of Corinth from the top are the reason people photograph this place.
itinerary.evening: Back down to Arachova. The village's bars fill from about 20:00 and do not empty; **Taverna Panagiota** for dinner first, then whichever bar on the main street has the crowd.
itinerary.dayStats: Arachova-Kelaria 27 km / 35-45 min / Kelaria base ≈ 1,750 m / weekday ticket €20, weekend €35 / lifts 08:30-16:00 high season, 09:00-15:00 low

itinerary.title: Delphi, the Charioteer, and a deliberate non-ski day
itinerary.morning: Do not ski. Drive 10 km west to **Delphi** and be at the gate when it opens. Walk the Sacred Way up past the treasuries to the **Temple of Apollo**, then on to the theatre and the stadium at the top, in February you will have most of it to yourself, and snow on the Phaedriades cliffs above is worth the trip alone.
itinerary.afternoon: The **Delphi Archaeological Museum** and the bronze **Charioteer**, then walk 15 minutes east to the **Tholos at the Sanctuary of Athena Pronaia**, which is the building on every postcard. Lunch in Delphi village looking down the olive valley toward Itea.
itinerary.evening: Eat in Delphi rather than driving back hungry, **Taverna Vakhos** on the upper street has the view. Then back to Arachova for a quiet night.
itinerary.dayStats: Arachova-Delphi 10 km / 15 min / site plus museum 3-4 h minimum / combined ticket typically €12, €20 winter rate / zero vertical metres skied

itinerary.title: Fterolakka, Gerontovrachos and the full width of the centre
itinerary.morning: Start from the lower base at **Fterolakka**, roughly 1,640 m and more sheltered than Kelaria, and ski the linking terrain across the ridge. This is the whole of the ski centre in one traverse and it takes a morning.
itinerary.afternoon: If the wind allows, take the chair up into **Gerontovrachos**, the highest and most exposed sector at around 2,250 m, which holds the coldest snow and is the first thing to close. **Be back on your own base's side of the ridge by 15:00**, a wind hold on the connecting lift means the car-park shuttle.
itinerary.evening: Drive down the north side instead of back to Arachova and eat in **Agoriani (Eptalofos)** or **Polydrosos**, fir-forested villages with wood stoves, half Arachova's prices, and no fur coats at all.
itinerary.dayStats: Fterolakka ≈ 1,640 m, Gerontovrachos to ≈ 2,250-2,260 m / ≈ 23 km of piste, 17 lifts / vertical band ≈ 650 m / ridge turnaround 15:00

itinerary.title: Weather-contingency and rest day: Livadi, the Corycian Cave and warm food
itinerary.morning: This is the designed flex day, and on Parnassos it is more likely than anywhere else in this collection to become a forced one, if the mountain has not opened, or a southerly has stripped it, take it now. Drive up to the **Livadi plateau** above Arachova, around 1,100-1,200 m, and either sledge with the Greek families or fit snowshoes.
itinerary.afternoon: Snowshoe from Livadi to the **Corycian Cave (Korykion Antron)**, the enormous stalactite cavern that Pausanias described and that was sacred to Pan and the nymphs, a 3-4 hour round trip in snow, best done with a guide from **Trekking Hellas** or the local mountaineering club, because the plateau navigation is not obvious in cloud.
itinerary.evening: Back to Arachova and eat properly: **Taverna Kaplanis** for slow-cooked meat, more formaela, and the local hilopites. Buy a rug or a length of woven cloth in one of the village workshops on the way.
itinerary.dayStats: Livadi plateau ≈ 1,100-1,200 m / Corycian Cave round trip 3-4 h on snowshoes / guided day ≈ €50, €90 pp / no EAWS avalanche bulletin in Greece, guide advised

itinerary.title: Best-conditions ski day, or the tour to Liakoura
itinerary.morning: Keep this day flexible and spend it wherever the mountain is best. If the snow has come good, this is the day to ski Kelaria and Gerontovrachos properly and to take the **4-day combined ticket at €95** if you have not already, it pays for itself on the third day.
itinerary.afternoon: If conditions are settled and you have booked a guide, the alternative is the **ski tour or winter ascent to Liakoura, the 2,457 m summit of Parnassos**, from the top of the lifts: a modest skin in good weather, a serious mountain day in bad. The view takes in the Gulf of Corinth, Giona, Vardousia and, on the clearest days, the Peloponnese.
itinerary.evening: Last night in Arachova. Start with tsipouro and mezedes somewhere on the main street, then dinner wherever the locals are, which will not be the place with the English menu outside.
itinerary.dayStats: Liakoura 2,457 m / summit day 4-6 h round trip from the lifts / 4-day combined ticket €95 / guide €150, €300 per group per day

itinerary.title: Down the mountain, and back to Athens
itinerary.morning: If the lifts are turning and your flight is late, take a **€15 low-season afternoon ticket** for a final couple of hours, Parnassos's short hours mean a morning-only ski is a genuinely good-value option here.
itinerary.afternoon: Return hire gear and chains in Arachova, then drive back to **ATH**: 200 km, 2 h 30-3 h, and add an hour if it is a Sunday evening in February, when the whole of Athens is coming down this road at once.
itinerary.evening: Fly out, or spend the last night in Athens, the drive is manageable but the Sunday return traffic on the Athens-Lamia motorway is the single most reliably unpleasant part of this trip.
itinerary.dayStats: Half-day afternoon ticket €15 low season / €20 high / Arachova-ATH 200 km / 2 h 30-3 h, +1 h Sunday evening / allow 2 h 30 at ATH

accommodationStrategy.name: Xenonas Generali
accommodationStrategy.description: A stone *xenonas* in the old part of the village, with fireplaces, thick walls and the sort of breakfast that assumes you are going up a mountain. It puts you inside walking distance of the tavernas and bars, which matters, because Arachova's streets are narrow, vertical and impossible to park on. Roughly €80, €140 per room.

accommodationStrategy.name: Domotel Anemolia Mountain Resort
accommodationStrategy.description: The comfortable option, set on the ridge with pool, spa and a long view down the Pleistos valley toward the sea. Choose it for the parking, the family space and the ability to reach both Delphi and the ski road quickly without navigating Arachova's lanes. Roughly €110, €200 per room.

accommodationStrategy.name: Polydrosos or Eptalofos guesthouses
accommodationStrategy.description: The counter-strategy: sleep on the quiet, forested northern flank of Parnassos, pay 30-40% less, eat better and more cheaply, and approach the ski centre from the north road. The cost is distance from Delphi and total absence of nightlife, which for many travellers is the point. Roughly €50, €90 per room.

logistics.connectivity: Coverage is good in Arachova, Delphi and at the ski bases, patchy on the Livadi plateau and absent in the Corycian Cave approach. Greece is **inside EU roaming**, so EU and most UK bundles apply at home rates. Download offline maps for the plateau.
logistics.emergency: **112** works nationally; **166** is the ambulance (EKAB) and **199** the fire service. Mountain rescue is provided by **EMAK**, the fire service's special disaster response unit, and the volunteer **Hellenic Rescue Team**; helicopter availability is weather- and asset-dependent and cannot be assumed. Greece is **in the EU**, so **EHIC/GHIC applies** to state healthcare, but not to rescue costs or repatriation. The nearest hospitals are at Amfissa and Livadeia.
logistics.weather: Parnassos lives and dies by Mediterranean cyclogenesis. A single depression tracking up the Ionian can deliver a metre in 48 hours; a warm **southerly (the *notias*)** behind it can take most of it away in a day. Wind is the other constant, **Gerontovrachos is exposed and closes on wind more often than on snow**, and the linking traverse between Kelaria and Fterolakka goes with it. Fog on the plateau is common and total. Check **snowreport.gr** and the ski centre's own bulletin every evening; do not plan more than a day ahead.
logistics.bookingWindows: Arachova beds for **Christmas-6 January and for weekends in February** need booking two to three months out and prices roughly double; midweek is available almost on the day. Lift tickets need no advance purchase, though the **5% online discount** is worth two minutes. Guided snowshoe or summit days should be arranged a week ahead. Delphi needs no booking in winter.
logistics.money: The **euro**. Cards are accepted in Arachova hotels and the larger tavernas; village kafeneia, the smaller north-side tavernas and some ski-centre kiosks prefer cash. ATMs exist in Arachova and Delphi. Tipping is rounding up, 5-10%.
logistics.transportRules: **Snow chains are a legal requirement on the Parnassos access road when conditions and signage demand, and this is actively enforced**, the police stop cars at the junction above Arachova and turn back those without them. Confirm your hire car carries a set, know how to fit them, and practise once in daylight. The Athens-Lamia motorway is tolled in several sections. Winter tyres are not legally mandated in Greece as they are in the Balkans, which makes chains all the more important. There is no vignette.
logistics.permits: The ski centre is on **state land managed by ETAD**; there is no separate park fee, but **parts of Parnassos are within a National Park and a Natura 2000 site**, which restricts off-road driving and camping. Drones need Greek civil aviation authorisation and are banned over the archaeological sites, Delphi in particular, where staff will intervene. Photography rules at Delphi permit personal stills but not tripods without permission.
logistics.health: Tap water in Arachova and Delphi is potable. **Greece publishes no daily EAWS avalanche bulletin**, the **EMY (Hellenic National Meteorological Service)** issues mountain weather forecasts and the ski centre issues a snow bulletin, but there is no five-point hazard rating for Parnassos. Treat all off-piste and touring as unbulletined, carry transceiver, shovel and probe, and go with someone who knows the mountain. Thin cover over rock is the most common cause of injury here in a poor year, ski conservatively on the marked routes when the base is shallow.

proTips: **Ski Monday to Friday and sightsee at weekends**, the inverse of every other resort in this collection. A weekday lift ticket is €20 against €35 at weekends, and Arachova on a Saturday belongs to Athens.
Take the **4-day combined ticket at €95** if you intend to ski three or more days. Against €35 weekend days it pays for itself immediately, and against €20 weekdays it still wins on the fourth.
**Buy your ticket online for the 5% electronic discount** and to avoid the window queue, which on a snowy Saturday is the longest line on the mountain.

Structure the week so that **the skiing is optional**. Parnassos may not open, may open only at weekends, or may open with two lifts. Delphi, the Corycian Cave and the north-side villages do not depend on snow, and a week built around them with skiing on top never fails.
**Hire skis in Arachova, not at the base.** They are cheaper, better fitted, and available, the Kelaria and Fterolakka shops are picked clean by 09:30 on a busy day.
**Fit the chains once in daylight in the hotel car park** before you need them on a dark, sleeting road. The police check at the junction above Arachova is routine and unsympathetic.

Cross the ridge back to your own base by **15:00**. Parnassos's lift hours are short, 16:00 in high season, 15:00 in low, and a wind hold on the linking chair means a shuttle between car parks in ski boots.

Eat on the **north side of the mountain** at least twice. Agoriani (Eptalofos) and Polydrosos have wood-fired tavernas at half Arachova's prices, and the fir forest up there is a completely different mountain from the bare southern slopes.

Go to **Delphi at opening time on a weekday in February**. The site takes snow beautifully, the tour buses do not run, and you will have the Temple of Apollo essentially alone, which is not a sentence that can be written about it in any other season.

raw.Pass tiers by name: There is one product and one operator: the **Parnassos Ski Centre**, run by the state property company **ETAD**, sells a single-resort ticket with no area or regional super-pass, there is nothing else within range to link to. The pricing is by **day of the week, not by season band**: **high season (weekends and public holidays) €35 adult**, **low season (weekdays) €20 adult**, the sharpest weekday/weekend spread in European skiing. **Afternoon tickets** (after 13:00 in high season, 12:00 in low) are **€20 and €15**. A **family ticket is €70** in high season. **School students pay €20 / €10** and **university students €35 / €20**. The nearest thing to a multi-day product is a **combined 4-day ticket at €95**, which is the value buy for anyone skiing more than two days. The **season pass is €450 individual, €1,000 for a "family plus"**. There is no dynamic pricing and no early-bird, but there is a **5% discount for buying electronically online** rather than at the window. **Lockers run €30, €250** depending on duration, and **instructor season passes €600, €1,000**. Operating hours are **08:30-16:00 in high season, 09:00-15:00 in low season**, which is short by Alpine standards and worth planning around. **There is no night skiing at Parnassos**, budget no floodlit supplement.
raw.Lift network and interconnects: Two sectors work as one. **Fterolakka**, the lower and more sheltered base at roughly **1,640 m**, and **Kelaria**, the main base at around **1,750 m**, are linked on snow across the ridge between them and are the whole of the everyday skiing. Above and east sits **Gerontovrachos**, the highest and most exposed sector, reached by chair from the Kelaria side and the first thing to shut in wind. The signature lift is the **Ermis (Hermes) gondola at Kelaria, the first and still one of the only gondola lifts in a Greek ski resort**, with the **Iraklis** chair and a further dozen or so chairs and conveyors making up a fleet of roughly **17 lifts**. **The two base areas are connected by road as well as by piste**, and the ski centre runs a shuttle between the Kelaria and Fterolakka car parks; that shuttle is what saves you when the linking traverse is closed by wind, which is often. **Last lifts are 16:00 in high season and 15:00 in low season**, and the practical rule is that **you must be back on your own base's side of the ridge by about 15:00**, because a wind hold on the connecting chair leaves you facing a car-park shuttle in ski boots.
raw.Snow reliability: This is the central problem and the file should not pretend otherwise. Parnassos spans roughly **1,600 m at the Fterolakka base to about 2,250-2,260 m at the top of Gerontovrachos**, a vertical band of only 650-670 m, on a mountain 25 km from the Gulf of Corinth at latitude 38°N. Aspects are mostly north and northeast, which is what makes the resort viable at all. Snowfall arrives in large, infrequent dumps from Mediterranean depressions and can vanish in a single warm southerly. **Snowmaking exists but covers only a fraction of the terrain, and the ski centre does not publish coverage as a percentage of pisted kilometres, do not quote one.** **Season: mid-December to early April**, but the reliable window is roughly 20 January to 28 February. **In a bad snow year Parnassos may open only at weekends, may run only the upper Kelaria and Gerontovrachos lifts, and in the worst years opens very late or barely at all**, which is exactly why this itinerary front-loads Delphi and the villages and treats every ski day as conditional. Check **snowreport.gr** and the ski centre's own daily bulletin the night before, every night.
raw.Off-piste and touring: The lift-served off-piste is the open ground on the **Gerontovrachos** flanks and the gullies between the Kelaria and Fterolakka pistes, short, and rocky when thin. The real objective is the **ski tour to Liakoura, the summit of Parnassos at 2,457 m**, from the top of the lifts: a straightforward but exposed skin in good conditions and a serious undertaking in bad ones, with weather that turns faster than anywhere in the Alps. Across the valley, **Giona** and **Vardousia** offer bigger and wilder touring for those with a guide and a week to spare. **Greece publishes no national daily avalanche bulletin on the EAWS scale.** The available sources are the **Hellenic National Meteorological Service (EMY, emy.gr)** for mountain weather, the ski centre's own snow bulletin, and **snowreport.gr**. Rescue is the **Hellenic Rescue Team (Ελληνική Ομάδα Διάσωσης)** and **EMAK**, the fire service's special disaster unit. **Take a guide.** The mountaineering clubs, **EOS Amfissas** and the Athens EOS, and commercial operators such as **Trekking Hellas** run guided winter ascents and snowshoe days; freelance-touring on Parnassos without local knowledge is how people get killed on a mountain that looks benign.
raw.Piste breakdown: The published figure is around **23 km in total: roughly 17 km easy (about 72%), 6.5 km intermediate (28%), and no officially graded black runs**, plus around 10 km of ungroomed marked ski routes, over some 19-20 named pistes and 17 lifts. **Beginners** are extremely well served, this is a resort of wide, gentle, sunny blue terrain and it is a genuinely good place to learn, with cheap weekday lift tickets to match. **Intermediates** get the Kelaria reds and the Gerontovrachos sector and will have seen everything in a day and a half. **Experts** should come for the ski tour to Liakoura and the view, not for the pistes; there is no lift-served steep skiing here in the Alpine sense, and anyone told otherwise has been sold something.
raw.Non-ski days: This is where the week earns its keep. **Delphi**, 10 km west of Arachova, is one of the great archaeological sites of the world, the Temple of Apollo, the theatre, the stadium and the **Delphi Archaeological Museum** with the bronze Charioteer, all of it near-empty in February and spectacular under snow. The **Livadi plateau** above Arachova at around 1,100-1,200 m is the local sledging and snow-play ground and the trailhead for the snowshoe walk to the **Corycian Cave (Korykion Antron)**, the huge stalactite cavern sacred to Pan and the nymphs. On the north side, **Agoriani (officially Eptalofos)** and **Polydrosos** are fir-forested villages with tavernas and a fraction of Arachova's prices. And Arachova itself has the **Church of Agios Georgios** at the top of its 264 steps, the weaving and rug workshops, and a food culture built on **formaela**, the PDO sheep's cheese fried at the table, and **tsipouro**.
raw.Hire, lockers and schools: Rental is available at both **Kelaria** and **Fterolakka** base areas and, better and cheaper, from the ski shops along Arachova's main street, expect roughly **€15, €25/day** for a standard ski-boot-pole package and **€70, €120 for six days**. Lockers at the ski centre run **€30, €250** depending on the rental period. Ski schools operate out of both bases; expect roughly **€40, €60 an hour for a private lesson** and **€150, €250 for a five-morning group course**, with English widely spoken. Two practical notes: **hire your snow chains at the same time as your skis** if the car did not come with them, and **rent in Arachova rather than at the base**, the base shops run out on a busy Saturday by 09:30.

sources.verified: Parnassos Ski Centre's published 2025-26 price list in EUR, day tickets at €35 in high season (weekends and holidays) and €20 in low season (weekdays); afternoon tickets at €20 high / €15 low, valid after 13:00 high season and 12:00 low; family ticket €70 high season; school-student tickets €20 / €10 and university-student tickets €35 / €20; a combined 4-day ticket at €95; individual season pass €450 and "family plus" €1,000; locker rentals €30, €250 by duration; ski-instructor passes €600, €1,000; a 5% discount for electronic/online ticket purchase; and operating hours of 08:30-16:00 in high season and 09:00-15:00 in low season. The ski centre's state management by ETAD. Greece's EU membership and therefore EU roaming and EHIC/GHIC applicability.
sources.confidenceNotes: **The altitude range is not settled.** One authoritative aggregator gives 1,581-2,250 m with a 669 m vertical; the resort and local sources are commonly quoted at 1,640-2,260 m. The text uses banded figures (≈1,640 m Fterolakka base, ≈1,750 m Kelaria base, ≈2,250-2,260 m top of Gerontovrachos) and these must be confirmed against ETAD's own technical data before publishing. **Individual lift names beyond the Ermis (Hermes) gondola are not fully verified**, the Iraklis chair is named on good authority but the full fleet naming and the exact lift serving Gerontovrachos should be checked against the current trail map. **No snowmaking coverage figure is published and none is asserted here.** **Season dates are indicative and unusually volatile at this resort**, in poor years opening slips by weeks and sectors run only at weekends; the daily source of truth is the ski centre bulletin and snowreport.gr. Delphi's winter combined-ticket price (€12, €20) is a band, not a quoted figure, and the reduced winter rate should be checked with the Ephorate. Rental, ski-school, guide and snowshoe prices are indicative bands. Arachova and Delphi hotel and taverna names are real and long-established but seasonal opening should be confirmed. The snow-chain enforcement described is a real and current practice on the access road but the legal citation should be re-checked against the Greek Highway Code before publishing as law.
